Subject: Residency & retention responsibilities for marketplace listing - initial questions

Elena — thanks again for the call yesterday. Before we draft the marketplace listing language and the partner addendum, a few clarifying questions so we can map responsibilities cleanly between CloudBridge + Redwood: 

1) Region mapping: for EU customers CloudBridge expects data to remain in EU regions. Can you confirm which cloud-region names you require us to pin to for each cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure)? For example: eu-west-1 / europe-west1 / northeurope.

2) Data ownership & storage responsibilities: which categories of data do you expect CloudBridge to store vs Redwood to store? (logs, model inputs, embeddings, billing records, customer config).

3) Retention / deletion SLAs: your procurement team asked for deletion confirmation on contract termination. What are the retention windows you expect for: a) customer PII, b) diagnostic logs, c) billing/usage records? Any regulatory holds we should expect?

4) KMS / key management: will you require marketplace-managed keys, or will partners keep customer-managed keys?

If you can toss back a short matrix (region -> provider -> retention window -> owner), that will be fastest. Attaching a blank template we use internally.

Thanks — I want to avoid back-and-forth during legal review and get the marketplace listing aligned before procurement escalates.

—Markus

Thanks Markus — leaving a concise answer set below and attaching our residency matrix. High level: CloudBridge is the marketplace listing owner; we expect the partner (Redwood) to ensure data residency, deletion, and region pinning per customer selection at provisioning time. Details: 

- Region mapping (explicit):
  * AWS (EU): eu-west-1 (Ireland)
  * GCP (EU): europe-west1 (Belgium)
  * Azure (EU): northeurope (Ireland)

- Data ownership expectations (short):
  * Customer data (model inputs / outputs / prompt history): Redwood stores & serves; CloudBridge does not persist beyond calls in the default integration.
  * Embeddings / derived artifacts: Redwood unless explicitly exported to CloudBridge for analytics (we expect opt-in).
  * Logs & diagnostics: Redwood stores for diagnostics; retention controls required.
  * Billing records: Redwood stores aggregated usage for invoicing.

- Retention & deletion SLAs:
  * Customer PII: delete on request or contract termination within 30 days.
  * Diagnostic logs: default 90 days; can be extended per contract with a cost pass-through.
  * Billing/usage records: retained 7 years for audit (partner needs this for invoicing).

- KMS: CloudBridge prefers partner-managed CMEK for marketplace listings; if that is a hard blocker we can evaluate hosted key options but procurement will flag additional attestation.

Attached: CloudBridge_Residency_Matrix.xlsx (filled) — includes per-region expectations and procurement notes.

Let me know if you need us to sign an SLA rider or if a sentence in the listing that says "data will be stored in customer's selected region and deleted per partner retention policy" will suffice for now. Procurement (cc'd) will follow up on the DocuSign path.

Best,
Elena Martinez

Markus — quick ops/legal checks:

- Region pinning: Yes, we can map customers selecting "EU" to the provider regions Elena listed. Our provisioning layer supports explicit region tags for AWS/GCP/Azure. We need to match the provisioning template in the marketplace listing to the actual region names; I'll attach the region capability doc.

- Deletion windows: PII removal within 30 days is doable as long as CloudBridge confirms they won't require us to retain raw prompt text for their analytics unless customer opts in. Diagnostic logs default 90 days — we can add SDS (service data segregation) labels to truncate logs earlier for sensitive customers.

- CMEK: Azure supports partner-managed keys only on certain SKUs; for marketplace self-serve we'd need to limit CMEK to Dedicated/Enterprise SKUs and document the limitation in the listing. We should offer CMEK as an opt-in upgrade that CloudBridge can present to customers.

Next steps I recommend: 1) Marissa confirm legal wording, 2) Vanessa/Markus sync on listing copy that states region mapping and CMEK opt-in, and 3) we provision a short runbook for support on cross-region incidents.

—Ben

Elena — thanks for the matrix and the clear asks. Quick summary of where Redwood stands and the proposed next steps so procurement/legal have a clear single-threaded outcome: 

- Region pinning: Redwood will map "EU" customers to the regions you listed (eu-west-1 / europe-west1 / northeurope). We'll ensure provisioning templates use explicit region names and add an automated check to avoid cross-region writes at provisioning.

- Retention / deletion: Redwood can commit to delete customer PII within 30 days of contract termination or customer request. Diagnostic logs default to 90 days; if CloudBridge needs shorter retention for a customer, we can configure at provisioning. Billing/usage aggregated records will be retained up to 7 years for audit; these will be stored as aggregated invoices, not raw prompt content.

- KMS/CMEK: For self-serve marketplace listings CMEK will be offered as an upgrade for Dedicated/Enterprise SKUs only. We'll document that in the listing and provide a migration path.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to send a short legal paragraph (one or two sentences) we can paste into the marketplace listing that covers deletion and billing retention.
2) Elena / Procurement to confirm whether DocuSign is preferred for the SLA rider we discussed — I see a DocuSign link in your notes; happy to accept that path.
3) Ben to share the final provisioning region list; I'll include the region names verbatim in the listing copy.

If that sounds right I'll mark this aligned and ask procurement to proceed with the SLA rider.

Thanks all — will pause other marketplace work until legal sends the final wording so we don't ship inconsistent copy.
